title: HB 472 (2023-2024 (135th General Assembly)): H. B. No. 472: Regards voter registration, voting, and voting systems
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) R.C. 3505.18(A)(1)
(quote) When an elector appears in a polling place to vote, the elector shall announce to the precinct election officials the elector's full name and current address and provide photo identification. (reprinted existing law)
(section) R.C. 3501.01(AA)(1)
(quote) "Photo identification" means one of the following documents that includes the individual's name and photograph and is not expired: (a) An Ohio driver's license, state identification card, or interim identification form issued by the registrar of motor vehicles or a deputy registrar under Chapter 4506. or 4507. of the Revised Code; (b) A United States passport or passport card; (c) A United States military identification card, Ohio national guard identification card, or United States department of veterans affairs identification card.
(section) R.C. 3505.18(B)(2)
(quote) The precinct election officials shall compare the elector's or attorney in fact's signature under division (B)(1) of this section with the image of the elector's or attorney in fact's signature included in the pollbook and shall compare the elector's appearance with the photograph of the elector on the elector's photo identification.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) R.C. 3505.18(A)(2)
(quote) If an elector does not have or is unable to provide photo identification to the precinct election officials, the elector may cast a provisional ballot under section 3505.181 of the Revised Code. (reprinted existing law)
(section) R.C. 3505.181(B)(7)(a)
(quote) For a provisional ballot to be eligible to be counted when it is cast by an individual who does not have photo identification because the individual has a religious objection to being photographed, the individual shall complete an affidavit of religious objection under section 3505.19 of the Revised Code. ... If the individual does not complete the affidavit at the time of casting the provisional ballot, the individual may appear at the office of the board of elections within four days after the day of the election and complete the affidavit. (reprinted existing law)
(section) R.C. 3505.181(B)(7)(b)
(quote) For a provisional ballot to be eligible to be counted when it is cast by any other individual who does not have or is unable to provide photo identification to the election officials, the individual who cast that ballot, within four days after the day of the election, shall appear at the office of the board of elections and provide photo identification. (reprinted existing law)
(section) R.C. 3505.19(A)
(quote) An elector who does not have photo identification because the elector has a religious objection to being photographed may complete an affidavit of religious objection in lieu of providing photo identification for the purpose of registering to vote, casting a provisional ballot, or casting an absent voter's ballot. (words 'registering to vote' and 'or casting an absent voter's ballot' are new)
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) R.C. 3509.03(B)(5)
(quote) The elector's Ohio driver's license or state identification card number or, if the elector does not have an Ohio driver's license or state identification card number and the elector submits a valid affidavit of religious objection to being photographed, the last four digits of the elector's social security number;
(section) R.C. 3509.03(B)(5)(c)
(quote) STRUCK: (c) A copy of the elector's photo identification.
(section) R.C. 3509.03(B)(6)
(quote) If the elector has a religious objection to being photographed, a valid affidavit of religious objection to being photographed shall be submitted.
(d_proof_of_citizenship)
(section) R.C. 3503.14(A)(7)(a) (registration form)
(quote) I declare under penalty of election falsification that: (a) I am a citizen of the United States, as evidenced by: (i) A valid and unexpired U.S. passport; or (ii) A certified copy of: U.S. birth certificate, Certification of Report of Birth, Consular Report of Birth Abroad, Certificate of Citizenship, or Certificate of Naturalization.
(section) R.C. 3503.201(A)(4)
(quote) Verify that the person is a United States citizen by comparing the person's information against the information in all of the following: (a) The database of the bureau of motor vehicles, as provided by the secretary of state and accessible to the board of elections; (b) The systematic alien verification for entitlements service, or its successor service, operated by the United States department of homeland security or its successor department; (c) A government database or a commercial service that contains information derived from individuals' (i) valid and unexpired United States passports or (ii) certified copies of United States birth certificates, certifications of reports of birth, consular reports of birth abroad, certificates of citizenship, or certificates of naturalization.
(section) R.C. 3503.201(B)(2)
(quote) If the board's staff are unable to verify one or more elements listed in division (A) of this section, the staff shall not register the person or update the person's registration, as applicable, but shall refer the application or update form to the board of elections for further evaluation.
(section) R.C. 3503.153(A)(4)(b)(i)
(quote) Add a notation in the elector's voter registration record that the next time the elector votes, the elector must cast a provisional ballot. In order for the elector's provisional ballot to be counted, the elector shall provide to the board of elections (I) a valid and unexpired United States passport, or (II) a certified copy of: United States birth certificate, certification of report of birth, consular report of birth abroad, certificate of citizenship, or certificate of naturalization.
(section) R.C. 3503.153(A)(4)(b)(ii)
(quote) Send a confirmation notice with return notice and cancellation notice requesting that the elector, within fifteen days, either provide a document to the board to confirm that the elector is a United States citizen or cancel the elector's voter registration.
(section) R.C. 3505.183(B)(4)(a)(xii)
(quote) The board has been unable to confirm using bureau of motor vehicles records, a government database, or a commercial service that the individual is a United States citizen. If the board is unable to confirm the individual's citizenship, the board shall notify the individual that the individual's ballot will be eligible to be counted only if the individual appears at the office of the board not later than the fourth day after the day of the election and provides one of the following: (I) A valid and unexpired United States passport; (II) A certified copy of one of the following: a United States birth certificate, certification of report of birth, consular report of birth abroad, certificate of citizenship, or certificate of naturalization.
(e_other_rule)
(section) R.C. 3503.201 (poll notice)
(quote) Voters must bring photo identification to the polls in order to verify identity. Eligible voters who do not provide photo identification will still be able to cast a provisional ballot.
(section) R.C. 3503.14(A)(5) (registration form)
(quote) Provide your Ohio driver's license or state identification card number or, if you do not have an Ohio driver's license or state identification card, and you submit a valid affidavit of religious objection to being photographed, the last four digits of your Social Security number
(section) R.C. 3503.15
(quote) A requirement that any person who has the authority to administer, or create, modify, or cancel any record in, the statewide voter registration database be a United States citizen and a resident of this state and have no criminal record involving dishonesty, moral turpitude, or any violation of election or immigration laws.
(other) 3501.01: new definitions (voter registration agency, pollbook)
(other) 3503.10, 3503.11: voter registration agencies must hand out an information sheet saying who is a citizen; agencies tell non-citizens they cannot register
(other) 3503.13, 3503.15: pollbooks hold signature images; no signature or photo images in the statewide database; permanent record retention
(other) 3503.151-3503.155: data-sharing and weekly reports (deaths, incompetence, felony convictions, non-citizen flags, movers)
(other) 3503.201 (new): staff verify each registration (name, birth date, citizenship, address, living, duplicate)
(other) 3503.231 (new): pollbook rules
(other) 3505.20: challenge procedure (compare photo and signature)
(other) 3506.xx: voting system and electronic pollbook rules and certification
(other) 3509.xx, 3511.xx: absentee application in ink; photo comparison for mail ballots; envelope text lists acceptable photo ID
(other) 3513.xx, 3599.12, 4507.53, 111.26, 111.44: petitions, penalties, BMV and confidential-record changes
(other) note: Large omnibus bill. The saved text is word-for-word identical to S.B. 274 (135th GA) after the enacting clause (word diff found no difference). Photo ID at polls, provisional ballot and four-day cure are existing law reprinted; the new rules are the citizenship database checks, the passport or certified-document proof required only from people a check flags, the religious-objection affidavit extended to registration and mail ballots, and removing 'copy of photo ID' as a mail ballot option. Sole version. Registration form asks for a sworn statement naming the documents; it does not require attaching them.
